newsitem.title: USA: Torotel finds product testing discrepancies.
newsitem.headline: Torotel finds product testing discrepancies.

text.p: Torotel Inc said Monday its Torotel Products Inc subsidiary in all likelihood failed to perform some required "thermal shock" testing as frequently as required and has inaccurately certified that all required testing had been performed.

New management at Torotel, which found the discrepancies, said it has made immediate corrections and believes its products now fully comply with testing requirements. Torotel said it disclosed its findings to the U.S. Department of Defense and expects to cooperate with any governmental investigation.

Torotel Products has contracts with multiple private corporations to supply components on Defense Department acquisitions. Some contracts require a "thermal shock" test be performed on 100 percent of certain electronic components.

Torotel Products' shipping statements certify that all mandated tests were performed. The company said Monday these deficiencies have been identified and corrected, though the company may be exposed to legal penalties and damages.
As a result of these apparent testing failures and false certifications, holders of certain Torotel Products' material contracts could have various claims against the company.

In addition, Torotel said the Department of Defense could have similar claims against Torotel Products, possibly materially hurting Torotel's business, assets, as well as revenues and income from continuing operations.

Separately, Torotel said the potential sale of its common stock by the company and its founder's family to Brockson Investment Co of Phoenix, Ariz. is under review. If these transactions are completed, Brockson would acquire more than 50 percent of Torotel's outstanding shares.
Torotel makes power switching supplies and magnetic components for commercial and military electronics.
